entities.name: Franciscus Irenicus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Franciscus Irenicus (Franz Friedlieb; 1494–1553) was a German humanist, Protestant-leaning historian, and pedagogue whose Germaniae exegeseos volumina sought to elevate German antiquities within Renaissance historical culture. Educated in the Erfurt and Heidelberg orbits, he mixed chorography, classical comparison, and reformist sympathies.

His project to give Germany a learned past paralleled Italian antiquarianism while serving emerging confessional identities. Teaching and historical compilation tied him to the Upper Rhine’s scholarly networks.

Irenicus illustrates how humanism nationalised antiquity for German readers.
